payload.question_text: Which statements describe batch job scheduling? Select all that apply.

options.error_type: Confuses batch scheduling with real-time transcription
options.rationale: Text during live speech describes real-time transcription. Batch jobs process stored recordings on a best-effort schedule.
options.better_fit: Expect text during speech when using real-time transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: A producer could promise live results that a batch job does not provide.
feedback.instructional: Batch scheduling concerns later processing, not transcription while someone speaks.

options.rationale: Batch jobs are scheduled on a best-effort basis. Their start timing is not guaranteed.
A batch job normally starts within minutes after the request. This is common timing, not a promise.
There is no guaranteed time when the job changes to running. Best-effort scheduling allows that uncertainty.

payload.explanation: Correct. Batch jobs are best-effort: they commonly start within minutes, but the running time is not guaranteed.

payload.question_text: Which method fits live incoming speech that needs text now?

options.rationale: Live incoming speech needs text while the person speaks. Real-time transcription is designed for that timing.

options.error_type: Confuses live speech with stored recordings
options.rationale: Batch transcription processes stored recordings. Its results can arrive later rather than during live speech.
options.better_fit: Use batch transcription when recordings already exist and later results are acceptable.

feedback.intrinsic: The person speaking now would not receive text when it is needed.
feedback.instructional: Choose real-time transcription for incoming live audio.

options.error_type: Confuses a storage URI with a transcription method
options.rationale: A SAS URI points batch transcription to audio in storage. It is not a method for converting incoming speech.
options.better_fit: Use a SAS URI to point batch transcription to stored audio files.

feedback.intrinsic: The live transcription need would remain unanswered.
feedback.instructional: A SAS URI identifies stored audio; it does not process live speech.

options.error_type: Confuses converting speech to text with converting text to speech
options.rationale: Text-to-speech converts written text into audible speech. The task requires spoken audio to become written text.
options.better_fit: Use text-to-speech when an application needs to read text aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: No live transcript would be created from the speaker’s words.
feedback.instructional: For speech becoming text, use transcription rather than text-to-speech.

payload.explanation: Correct. Real-time transcription returns text from live incoming speech as it happens.

payload.question_text: A batch transcription job has a guaranteed time when it changes to the running state.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A producer could make a timing promise that cannot be relied upon.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Batch transcription uses best-effort scheduling, so the change to running is not guaranteed.

payload.explanation: Correct. A batch job commonly starts within minutes, but there is no guaranteed running time.

payload.question_text: Use batch transcription when audio is already stored and results can arrive later.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A saved recording could be handled as if it needed immediate live text.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose batch transcription when audio already exists and receiving the transcript later is acceptable.

payload.explanation: Correct. Batch transcription is for stored recordings and asynchronous results.

payload.question_text: What converts incoming spoken audio to text as a person speaks?

options.error_type: Confuses live audio with stored recordings
options.rationale: Batch transcription processes recordings that already exist. Its results arrive after submission rather than during live speech.
options.better_fit: Use batch transcription for stored recordings when results can arrive later.

feedback.intrinsic: Captions would not appear while the person is speaking.
feedback.instructional: Choose real-time transcription when audio is arriving live.

options.rationale: Real-time transcription converts incoming speech into text while the person speaks. It is used when text is needed from live audio.
Speech synthesis converts text into spoken audio. It does not create written text from spoken input.
options.better_fit: Use speech synthesis when written content needs to be read aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The spoken words would still not become captions.
feedback.instructional: This task needs speech-to-text, not text-to-speech.

options.rationale: Translation changes content between languages. The need here is to convert spoken audio into text.
options.better_fit: Use speech translation when someone speaks one language and needs output in another.

feedback.intrinsic: The live speech would not be captured as a transcript.
feedback.instructional: First identify whether the task is speech-to-text or a language change.

payload.explanation: Correct. Real-time transcription receives live audio and returns text while speech is happening.

payload.question_text: Which statements describe batch transcription? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Batch transcription is for audio recordings that already exist. Those recordings can be on a file share, remote server, or Azure storage.

options.text: It needs a live microphone stream
options.error_type: Confuses stored recordings with live audio
options.rationale: A live microphone stream is used for real-time transcription. Batch transcription processes stored recordings.
options.better_fit: Use a live microphone stream for real-time transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would prepare live input even though the recordings already exist.
feedback.instructional: Batch work begins with stored audio, not a required live microphone stream.

options.rationale: Asynchronously means results arrive after the request is submitted. Batch transcription does not require an immediate result.

options.text: It can use audio in Azure storage
options.rationale: Batch transcription can process audio stored in Azure storage. A SAS URI can point to such audio files.

payload.explanation: Correct. Batch transcription processes stored audio and provides results later.

payload.question_text: Real-time transcription can be used when someone is speaking during a presentation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Captions would arrive too late for people following the presentation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Real-time transcription is intended for incoming speech, including presentations and demonstrations.

payload.explanation: Correct. A presentation is a live-speaking situation, so text can be returned as the person speaks.

payload.question_text: What can point batch transcription to audio files in storage?

options.error_type: Confuses an audio-file URI with a recognition object
options.rationale: A SpeechRecognizer performs transcription in an application. It is not the URI that points batch work to stored audio.
options.better_fit: Use a SpeechRecognizer to perform transcription after configuring audio input.

feedback.intrinsic: The stored file location would still be missing.
feedback.instructional: A SAS URI identifies audio in storage for batch transcription.

options.error_type: Confuses storage access with service connection
options.rationale: An endpoint connects an application to Azure Speech. It does not point batch transcription to an audio file in storage.
options.better_fit: Use an endpoint when initializing a connection to Azure Speech.

feedback.intrinsic: The batch request would not identify the stored recording.
feedback.instructional: Connection details and a stored-file URI have different roles.

options.rationale: A speech key is used for authentication. It is not a pointer to stored audio.
options.better_fit: Use a speech key with an endpoint to authenticate a connection.

feedback.intrinsic: The audio file location would still not be supplied.
feedback.instructional: Authentication proves access; a SAS URI points to the stored audio.

options.rationale: A shared access signature, or SAS, URI can point batch transcription to stored audio files. It is used with audio in storage.

payload.explanation: Correct. A SAS URI can point batch transcription to audio files in storage.

payload.question_text: Batch transcription converts an incoming microphone stream into text as a person speaks.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Someone waiting for live text could receive it only after later processing.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Batch transcription works with stored recordings and returns results asynchronously.

payload.explanation: Correct. Incoming microphone audio while a person speaks describes real-time transcription.

payload.question_text: A shared access signature (SAS) URI is a storage pointer, not a transcription method.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The task could assign transcription work to a URI that only identifies stored audio.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A SAS URI points batch transcription to stored audio, while the transcription service performs the conversion.

payload.explanation: Correct. A SAS URI identifies audio in storage for batch transcription; it does not perform transcription.
